sources_considered.why: The original November 2022 HELM paper directly evaluates disinformation generation.
Confirms the original version's publication date.
A 2022 GPT-3 evaluation supplies material evidence of useful claim-screening performance.
Confirms that the proceedings were published on August 9, 2022.
Read. Human recruitment occurred in 2022, but the timing of every model-evaluation component was not established sufficiently to use it decisively.
The original 2022 version concerns RoBERTa. The later version's GPT-family experiments cannot be backdated to 2022.

evidence_items.publisher: Stanford Center for Research on Foundation Models, via arXiv
evidence_items.explanation: The contemporary benchmark supports the generation half: leading models produced realistic headlines supporting supplied narratives. It does not establish that those models were generally poor at fighting misinformation.

evidence_items.publisher: Politecnico di Milano researchers, CEUR Workshop Proceedings
evidence_items.explanation: GPT-3 performed competitively on screening tasks that can assist fact-checkers, qualifying a broad dismissal of its usefulness. Detecting a checkable claim does not establish whether the claim is true, so this is not decisive evidence about factual verification.

unresolved_gaps: The located evidence does not jointly establish the claimed general asymmetry across generation, factual verification, and correction.
No ordinary, task-independent threshold separates 'poor' from useful but imperfect performance.
